headline: Is Election Day 2026 a federal holiday? Here's what open and closed on November 3
subheadline: US banks to operate normally on election day
author: Web Desk
article_text:
No, Election Day is not a federal holiday. Therefore, banks, stock exchanges, postal services, and most businesses will be working on November 3, when Americans vote in the last midterm elections of the second term of President Donald Trump.

What is open on Election Day?

Stock exchanges (New York Stock Exchange, NASDAQ), bond markets, and most banks will work according to their usual schedule.

The postal service will be working and delivering mail; UPS and FedEx will also be working, delivering and picking up packages and operating stores as usual. Major chains of supermarkets and other shops will be working.

What states have a holiday on Election Day?

Each state, not the federal government, regulates the status of Election Day. Five states, including Illinois, Hawaii, Maryland, New York, and West Virginia, have a public holiday on Election Day.

In which states must employers allow paid time off to vote?

There are fifteen states, including Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming, that mandate paid time off to vote on Election Day even though the day is not a public holiday in any of these states.

Ohio recognizes Election Day as a holiday from noon to 5:30 p.m., and employers are required to allow an appropriate amount of time off to vote, but state government operations remain open.

Stock exchanges (New York Stock Exchange, NASDAQ), bond markets, and most banks will work according to their usual schedule.

What states have a holiday on Election Day?

Each state, not the federal government, regulates the status of Election Day. Five states, including Illinois, Hawaii, Maryland, New York, and West Virginia, have a public holiday on Election Day.

In which states must employers allow paid time off to vote?

There are fifteen states, including Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming, that mandate paid time off to vote on Election Day even though the day is not a public holiday in any of these states.

headline: Oscar winner Michael Douglas looks back on secret romance with co-star
subheadline: In his memoir, Douglas shared how he would spend time with Kathleen Turner after filming
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Michael Douglas has finally opened up about a romance with Kathleen Turner that remained a secret for four years.

The actor revealed that their feelings for each other grew while they were working on the 1984 film Romancing the Stone in Mexico.

At the time, Douglas was separated from his wife, Diandra Luker. He has now admitted that he and Turner became more than just co-stars but tried hard to keep their relationship away from the public eye.

READ MORE: Michael Douglas explains why success should not be dismissed as family privilege

In his memoir, One Helluva Ride, Douglas shared how they used to spend time together after filming. He, however, also recalled secretly visiting Turner's hotel room at night, when everyone else go to sleep.

Their romance came to an end after Diandra visited Mexico with their son Cameron. She became suspicious about the two and Douglas said they decided to end things after her visit.

The Hollywood icon, moreover, later returned to his wife but admitted that their marriage was never the same again.

READ MORE: Raye enters Hollywood with major star packed project

Now, Douglas is using his experience to warn young actors about dating their co-stars. He believes things can become very uncomfortable when a relationship ends but both actors still have to work together.

Turner also reacted to the revelation, saying, "I love Michael, and I look forward to enjoying the book."

headline: FIFA boss Infantino accused of using Trump ties to secure US work permit for undocumented maid
subheadline: There is no public finding that the permit was improperly issued or that Infantino or Cordeiro broke the law
author: Web Desk
article_text:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino allegedly asked an adviser with connections to US President Donald Trump's administration to secure a work permit for his family's housekeeper after she lost her legal authorization to work in the country.

The allegations, reported by the New York Post on Tuesday, November 3, come as Trump's administration continues to tighten immigration rules for foreign nationals living and working in the United States.

According to leaked documents and three sources familiar with the matter, Infantino's Nicaraguan housekeeper, Yajarlin del Socorro Fernandez, remained on FIFA's payroll for months after her work authorisation was revoked in June 2025.

An internal FIFA employment letter reportedly confirmed that Fernandez worked full-time for the football governing body's American division from August 2024 until October 2025.

The 33-year-old had initially received permission to work under a humanitarian parole programme, which the Trump administration subsequently terminated for several nationalities, including Nicaraguans.

However, she received a fresh work permit in January 2026.

The newspaper alleged that Infantino sought assistance from Carlos Cordeiro, a former FIFA official who was appointed to Trump's White House World Cup task force in May 2025.

Cordeiro reportedly used his government connections to help Fernandez obtain new immigration authorization.

The report also alleged that an incorrect residential address had been used in her earlier immigration paperwork.

Immigration lawyer Michael Wildes, who previously represented First Lady Melania Trump, told the newspaper that securing a new permit under such circumstances would be highly unusual for an ordinary applicant.

However, there is no public finding that the permit was improperly issued or that Infantino or Cordeiro broke the law.

FIFA, Infantino and US immigration authorities did not respond to the newspaper's questions. Cordeiro said he was unaware of the story.

The allegations emerge amid growing scrutiny of Infantino's leadership ahead of FIFA's presidential election in March 2027.

headline: Meghan rubs salt into Harry's wounds as punishment for failure
subheadline: The Dychess of Sussex wants Harry to step up to lead from the front
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Meghan Markle has allegedly urged Prince Harry to finally take charge of the royal mess he once promised would never happen, rubbing salt into the Duke's wounds.

Harry is said to have been left heartbroken after being snubbed by King Charles as the Sussexes were expecting a warm welcome from the monarch on their return to Britain.

Contrary to the Duke's wishes, he was sidelined instead of being embraced by the monarch. Now, the Duchess is said to be taking a much firmer stance.

READ MORE: Who forced Meghan Markle to stay silent?

According to an insider close to the couple, Meghan already knew this would happen and had told her husband to leave no stone unturned to achieve excellence.

However, she is now exhausted by the never-ending cycle of royal drama and rejection. She feels Harry's pain but wants him to finally admit the truth and take responsibility.

Meghan's message to him is clear: "own the decision instead of living with regret."

Harry was sure and confident that he would mend the fractured family ties, but he failed to do so.

Now Meghan wants him to step up, lead from the front, and stop expecting the Palace to make the first move.

The Duchess has reportedly changed her stance and wants to end the royal rift and find a way forward rather than reliving the same painful snub all over again.

headline: 'Homeless' Nicolas Cage reveals current living arrangements
subheadline: The actor, 62, says he's 'a little bit homeless' after damage to his Malibu mansion
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Nicolas Cage is sharing an update on his living situation after a massive sinkhole damaged his Malibu mansion in September.

Speaking at L.A. Comic Con on Saturday, October 31, the 62-year-old actor revealed he won’t be able to accommodate Halloween trick-or-treaters because he’s “homeless.”

“I’m currently a little bit homeless,” Cage said. “Something happened to my house in Malibu so I’m just sort of living in hotels so I don’t have normal trick or treaters I would like to enjoy tonight.”

READ MORE: Nicolas Cage says goodbye to birth name in unexpected reveal

Despite the disruption, the National Treasure star planned to take his 4-year-old daughter, August, trick-or-treating in Santa Monica before settling down to watch Stanley Kubrick’s horror classic The Shining after she went to bed.

Cage’s $10.5 million beachfront property suffered severe damage in September after heavy rain and coastal erosion caused the ground to collapse around the home. Images showed a massive hole where the driveway once stood, with cracked asphalt and concrete swallowed by the sinkhole.

The damage also forced evacuations across the neighbourhood. According to the New York Post, seven nearby homes were deemed unsafe, while another 24 faced restrictions because emergency vehicles could no longer access the properties safely.

READ MORE: Nicolas Cage rushes to protect Malibu home as sinkhole grows

headline: Can hypnosis make you forget a movie? 30 volunteers to find out in November
subheadline: There is no guarantee the experiment will work
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Ever wished you could forget the ending of your favourite movie just to experience the surprise all over again? A cinema in the Netherlands is preparing to find out whether hypnosis can make that possible.

Dutch cinema chain Pathé has recruited 30 moviegoers for an unusual experiment in which a hypnotherapist will attempt to make them temporarily forget films they have already watched.

The experiment, called Pathe REWIND, will take place on November 9 at the company's Buitenhof cinema in The Hague.

Participants will undergo individual online hypnosis sessions with Victor Kraemer, a hypnotherapist with more than 30 years of experience, before receiving another session shortly before the screening.

They will then watch one of four films: The Matrix, Se7en, La La Land or Interstellar. The final selection will depend on participants' preferences.

The idea is to see whether viewers can experience familiar scenes, unexpected twists and emotional moments without remembering what happens next.

However, there is no guarantee the experiment will work.

Previous research has shown that hypnosis can temporarily interfere with people's ability to recall certain information, particularly among individuals who are highly responsive to hypnotic suggestions.

In one study, participants who were hypnotised struggled to remember details of a documentary they had watched, but their memories returned after the suggestion was reversed.

That does not mean hypnosis can erase an entire movie from someone's memory.

Pathé has acknowledged the uncertainty, describing the event as an experiment rather than a proven method of controlling memories.

Applications closed on October 29, with selected participants offered free admission.

For movie lovers who wish they could experience a favourite plot twist again without knowing it was coming, the results could be particularly interesting.

headline: 17 terrorists killed in two Balochistan IBOs, soldier martyred: ISPR
subheadline: Operations conducted in Kachhi, Kharan on reported presence of terrorists
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Ten terrorists killed during operation in Kachhi.
Seven more neutralised in separate Kharan IBO.
Sepoy Hikmat Ullah martyred during fire exchange.

RAWALPINDI: Security forces killed 17 terrorists in two intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts, while a soldier was martyred during an exchange of fire, the military’s media wing said on Tuesday.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the operations were conducted on November 1 following reports about the presence of terrorists belonging to what it described as the Indian proxies “Fitna Al Hindustan” and “Fitna Al Khawarij”.

In Kachhi district, security forces carried out an IBO in the Sanni area, where they thwarted an attempt by terrorists to establish a roadblock in the city through “proactive action”, the statement said.

Ten terrorists were killed during the operation, while weapons and ammunition were also recovered, according to the ISPR.

In a separate operation in Kharan district, security forces busted a terrorist hideout, leading to an intense exchange of fire in which seven terrorists were killed.

Weapons and ammunition were also recovered during the Kharan operation.

However, Sepoy Hikmat Ullah was martyred during the exchange of fire, the military’s media wing said. The 25-year-old soldier belonged to Karak district.

The ISPR said sanitisation operations were underway to eliminate any other terrorists found in the area.

It added that security forces and law enforcement agencies would continue their counterterrorism campaign under the “Azm-e-Istehkam” initiative approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan to eliminate foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.

In Kachhi district, security forces carried out an IBO in the Sanni area, where they thwarted an attempt by terrorists to establish a roadblock in the city through “proactive action”, the statement said.

Ten terrorists were killed during the operation, while weapons and ammunition were also recovered, according to the ISPR.

In a separate operation in Kharan district, security forces busted a terrorist hideout, leading to an intense exchange of fire in which seven terrorists were killed.

headline: Johnny Depp sets one major condition for his return as Jack Sparrow
subheadline: The last Pirates film came out in 2017
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Johnny Depp gave Pirates of the Caribbean fans a reason to hope that he can play Captain Jack Sparrow again.

The actor has made it clear that he is open to returning but he wants the next film to end the story in a way that makes fans happy.

In a recent interview with Entertainment Tonight, Depp explained that he would not return just to make another movie.

He wants his involvement to help give the popular series a better ending. After playing Jack Sparrow for so many years, he wants the character's story to finish on a good note.

READ MORE: Paul Bettany revisits Johnny Depp scandal

The actor, however, also talked about his friendship with producer Jerry Bruckheimer and said he still trusts him. “I will go to work with [Jerry] Bruckheimer tomorrow for anything. Doesn’t matter… if it’s Jerry, I trust him. We have a deep friendship.”

Bruckheimer also shared that he would like Depp to return even though the next film is being planned as a reboot.

He, moreover, been working on the new story with writer Jeff Nathanson and said the ending is already in good shape.

READ MORE: Oscar winner Michael Douglas looks back on secret romance with co-star

The last Pirates film came out in 2017. While no return has been confirmed, Depp's comments have once again raised hopes of seeing Jack Sparrow on screen.

headline: Donald the lame duck? Trump will have other ideas if he loses midterms
subheadline: Trump's post-midterms strategy could spark disruption on multiple fronts
author: AFP
article_text:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's second term has been a wild ride, but his last two years in power could be wilder still if Republicans lose control of Congress in Tuesday's US midterm elections.

From renewed military action against Iran to election challenges and fightbacks against Democratic investigations, Trump's post-midterms playbook could involve disruption on all fronts.

Analysts warn that Trump as a "lame duck" president could be the most vengeful Trump of all.

"I'm skeptical that President Trump will go quiet into that good night," Peter Loge, director of George Washington University's School of Media and Public Affairs, told AFP.

"There is nothing in history that says he will say 'I've been beaten, my time is over.' Every time Trump has been backed into a corner, he has shouted more and come out fighting."

Vetoes and vengeance

Trump has always viewed himself as a fighter. He has been clear he will take the same approach if Democrats win one or both chambers of Congress.

"If we didn't win, I veto everything" in any Democratic legislative agenda, Trump told the New York Post.

The White House says it is also ready to fight back against whatever investigations — or impeachment proceedings — Democrats throw at them.

"They'll probably go after me, and I'll go after them," Trump said in a Time magazine interview. Trump could even direct the Justice Department to investigate Democrats who are probing him.

Trump, who baselessly disputed his 2020 presidential election loss, could also interfere in the midterms by challenging counts or delaying the certification of disputed races.

Iran

Foreign policy is the one area in which lame-duck US presidents still have wide-ranging powers.

Trump may renew large-scale military operations against Iran, although he appeared to indicate on the eve of the midterms that fresh talks could produce a deal.

"I don't think he wants his legacy to be a warmonger. He wants his legacy to have left America stronger," Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution told AFP.

Speculation has swirled that Trump could fire Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth as the Iran war drags on — a familiar move for a president who never likes to take the blame.

Ukraine, detente and trade

Trump loves to think of himself as a master of peace deals and is likely to continue to push Ukraine to agree to a settlement with Russia. Fresh trilateral talks are set for next week.

At the same time, Trump will continue to seek detente with the leaders he views as his great power equals — Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The three will potentially meet at a summit in China later this month.

The US is also likely to continue its retrenchment from some of its NATO and other Western allies — and may even accelerate it, said Hass of the Brookings Institution.

On trade, however, Trump would likely remain "unrelentingly active," as shown by his recent hostility towards Canada, Hass said.

Staying relevant for 2028?

Trump loves being the center of attention and is unlikely to relish the spotlight turning towards potential successors in the 2028 US presidential election.

Trump — who hosted the reality television show "The Apprentice" — has been notably coy about backing either Vice President JD Vance or Secretary of State Marco Rubio for the top job.

But Trump has largely stopped dropping hints at running for a constitutionally-barred third term.

Allan Lichtman, a professor at American University and author of "Great American Presidents: The Twelve Who Transformed the Nation," said Trump would certainly "keep the focus on himself by being the kingmaker."

Monuments to himself

Like other people getting ready for retirement, Trump may choose to focus on home improvement.

In his closing midterms speech, Trump barely mentioned policy and instead talked about his renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and other plans to beautify Washington.

Trump has openly expressed a desire to stamp his own physical mark on Washington because he fears that others will not do it for him.

"We have a lot of great things planned for Washington," he said at the Reflecting Pool on Monday.

From renewed military action against Iran to election challenges and fightbacks against Democratic investigations, Trump's post-midterms playbook could involve disruption on all fronts.
Analysts warn that Trump as a "lame duck" president could be the most vengeful Trump of all.
"I'm skeptical that President Trump will go quiet into that good night," Peter Loge, director of George Washington University's School of Media and Public Affairs, told AFP.

Vetoes and vengeance

headline: King Charles acknowledges 'wrongs of past' but stops short of apology
subheadline: King Charles keynote speech at Commonwealth Summit: 'We cannot change the actions of those who came before us'
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles has finally acknowledged the “wrongs of the past" as he delivered a keynote speech at the Commonwealth Summit on Tuesday.

In an apparent nod to Britain's role in the slave trade, the King told the world leaders in his opening speech, “We cannot change the actions of those who came before us," adding: “We can, however, learn from the past."

Charles, the head of the Commonwealth, stopped short of a full apology amid calls for Britain to apologise and pay reparations.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who last week declared that he is "open" to Britain apologising for its slavery past, was also in attendance.

The King also added in his speech: “None of us, of course, would be here today were it not for our history, which has shaped us in myriad ways. History is not ours to choose or to change. It is bequeathed to us in complex synthesis by forebears we can never know. Our inheritance includes both their achievements and their failures – the good they did as well as the wrongs."

The monarch continued: “History can be hard to compass, viewed as it is through the prism of time, which can be both clarifying and distorting, and yet its consequences resonate with contemporary force. Our history inspires us, can appall us, yet it can always teach us.

“The transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other Members of our Commonwealth. As I have said before, that shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow.”

The 77-year-old said: “In fact, in a desperately troubled world, the Commonwealth has welcomed new members who see the unique value of this organisation and have chosen to be part of its future. All around us, trust between nations is under critical strain, as international norms and systems are tested to their limits.

“Brutal conflict stalks our world, destroying lives and casting long shadows across the globe. Technology is transforming our societies and our economies at dizzying speed, with little certainty about where it might lead us.

“As I have consistently tried to emphasise, climate change is no longer just a terrifying prospect, but a catastrophic reality which threatens our very way of life. Nature is under constant attack and critical natural systems are collapsing."

“The Commonwealth cannot provide all of the solutions. It does, however, offer an unparalleled opportunity to work together – across our societies and our economies, through our businesses, our institutions and our communities.”

He concluded by saying: “Today the leadership of this unique institution is in your hands. Each of you has the opportunity to make the greatest possible difference. I pray that over these coming days you will embrace this opportunity and commit yourselves to action.

“I pray that you will renew your determination to build a Commonwealth in which prosperity and Nature flourish side by side; in which investment builds resilience as well as social and economic capital; and in which trade creates opportunity from which everyone can benefit – especially those people in Member States in most need of those benefits, both economic and environmental.

“Above all, Ladies and Gentlemen, I trust that each of you will recommit yourselves to a Commonwealth in which our young people can look to the future with greater confidence and purpose. So that from this remarkable family of nations, our people can draw inspiration and hope – just as I, myself, have always done.”

“The transatlantic trade in enslaved persons still casts a shadow over these islands and other members of our Commonwealth. As I have said before, that shameful chapter of history is one that fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow.”

Charles said the more he had “furthered my own understanding of the issues, through listening, learning and looking.”

Prince William and Harry's father listed access to education, jobs and opportunities, as well as intra-Commonwealth trade and climate change resilience as ways of helping those “who struggle against hardship and disadvantage”.

“For, as any sailor navigating the seas knows, we cannot command the winds, least of all where the winds of yesterday have delivered us – but we can choose how we set our sail,” Charles said.

headline: Is Elon Musk preparing to take over Hollywood next?
subheadline: There are many documentaries about Elon Musk
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Elon Musk may be getting ready to make his mark on Hollywood after building huge businesses in other parts of the world.

The billionaire already made a name for himself through Tesla, SpaceX and X. Now, his growing interest in films left many people wondering what he wants to do next.

Musk reportedly invested around $1 billion in Skydance, the company which is led by David Ellison.

READ MORE: Alec Baldwin blasts Elon Musk for Lupita Nyong'o's ‘The Odyssey' criticism

The move came at a time when Hollywood is already dealing with major changes. Many people, however, in the film industry are also unsure about Musk's plans because of his close connection with Donald Trump.

His interest in making films has also become clear through Grok, his AI tool. It recently released a short version of The Odyssey, a famous Greek story about a man who leaves his family to fight in the Trojan War.

Musk wanted to create his own version after speaking against Christopher Nolan's take on the same story.

The short film, moreover, did not receive much praise from online viewers.

READ MORE: Johnny Depp sets one major condition for his return as Jack Sparrow

At the same time, a new documentary about Musk's life and career brought more attention to his growing power as well.

All of this raised a bigger question and that is, can Musk's next big move change Hollywood too?

headline: Americans bet nearly $1.9 billion on midterm elections as one trader eyes $30,000 profit
subheadline: Kalshi accounts for approximately $1.3 billion
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Americans have wagered nearly $1.9 billion on the midterm elections, turning the battle for control of Congress into a massive betting market where some traders stand to make tens of thousands of dollars.

Among them is Noah Poser, a 28-year-old financial technology worker who has placed six-figure wagers on the elections and could walk away with a profit of up to $30,000.

Poser, who is betting on a strong Democratic performance, plans to spend election night monitoring results from a friend's watch party in New York.

His approach is based on mathematical models rather than political loyalties, with bets placed months ago when the odds were more favourable.

Another trader, 22-year-old Florida State University student Yadin Eldar, has taken a different approach, backing Republican candidates in races where he believes their chances have been underestimated.

Eldar admitted that watching the numbers change can be stressful, saying he sometimes makes impulsive decisions when the markets move against him.

The surge in political betting has been driven by platforms including Kalshi and Polymarket, which allow users to trade contracts based on election outcomes.

A Washington Post analysis found that nearly $1.9 billion in trading activity had been recorded across the two platforms by Monday evening, with Kalshi accounting for approximately $1.3 billion.

The figures represent trading volume rather than the amount of cash individuals have deposited.

The platforms gained widespread attention during the 2024 presidential election, when their odds pointed towards Donald Trump's victory.

However, recent forecasting failures have raised questions about their reliability.

For traders, the stakes extend beyond predicting which party controls Congress. Election night could also determine whether months of speculation end in substantial profits or painful losses.

headline: Olivia Rodrigo's producer Dan Nigro confirms mystery after fan-theories
subheadline: Olivia Rodrigo and Dan Nigro finally reveal the biggest secret of 'yspsfagsil' era
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Olivia Rodrigo is about to release a new song she worked on with her longtime producer and friend Dan Nigro, take me home (4 christmas), and it had been in the vault for a long time.

The 23-year-old pop superstar appears to have recorded the song during the summer as Nigro later shared on his Instagram Stories.

The music producer also jokingly revealed that this was the one song he had been teasing all year when he told fans that the best song he has ever made with Rodrigo was not included on the album - you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love.

Taking to the comments, Nigro wrote, "This is definitely not my least favorite song we've ever made," and solved the mystery.

Fans flocked to X and reacted to the comment, writing, "WAIT DAN CONFIRMED HELLO," and "soo this is dan's favourite song they were talking about all this time i'm so seated."

Another added, "i already know it's gonna be so good," while one chimed in, "he knew we were detectives about this quote."

Someone noted, "he’s so funny for this im crying," and "omg this makes me even MORE excited!!!"

While one fan predicted, "ITS GONNA BE A HIT."

headline: Who is Mai Michael? Former elementary school teacher behind Crown New Materials's 787% debut
subheadline: Crown New Materials surges 787% in Shenzhen debut, minting two billionaires
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Crown New Materials Technology, a Zhongshan-based adhesives and tap maker, surges as much as 787% on its first trading day in Shenzhen on November 3, 2026, turning Chairman and CEO Mai Michael and his sister Mai Huixia into paper billionaires.

The stock opened at 56 yuan against an offer price of 16.98 yuan, lifting the company’s market capitalization to about 26.3 billion yuan ($3.7 billion), far above the roughly 7.96 billion yuan implied by the IPO price.

The rally triggered two temporary trading halts during the morning session.

Mai, 62, a former elementary school teacher who entered the materials business in 1985, holds a net worth of $2.5 billion based on his stake, according to Forbes estimates.

His sister Mai Huixia, 64 the company’s vice chairman, holds a fortune of about $2 billion.

Founded in 2000, Crown New Materials makes industrial-grade and electronic-grade adhesive materials and functional films used in consumer electronics, automobiles, new-energy batteries, and semiconductors.

Its customers include OPPO, vivo, Huawei, Apply, BYD, Tesla, and CATL. The company raised 956 million yuan ($144 million) in its IPO to expand production and build a research center.

Finances shows revenue raising from 2.895 billion yuan in 2023 to 3.408 billion yuan in 2025, with net profit growing from 278 billion to 309 million yuan. However, the company estimated first-three quarter 2026 net profit of 225 million to 244 million yuan, flat to down 7.98% year on year, indicating slowing earnings momentum.

headline: Pakistan successfully tests first indigenously developed Fa'az air-to-air missile
subheadline: Missile features advanced terminal guidance system to engage targets at longer ranges
author: Zarmeen Zehra
article_text:
Fa’az marks milestone in Pakistan’s defence capabilities.
Missile designed to engage longer-range aerial targets.
Test witnessed by military officers, scientists, engineers.

Pakistan has successfully conducted the flight test of its first indigenously developed Fa’az air-to-air missile, marking a significant advancement in the country’s aerospace and defence capabilities, the military’s media wing said on Tuesday.

According to a statement from the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the missile is equipped with a state-of-the-art terminal guidance system and is capable of engaging enemy aerial targets at longer ranges.

The Fa’az missile is expected to enhance the operational flexibility of the Pakistan Air Force (PAF) and further strengthen the country’s overall defence posture, the statement said.

It added that the successful flight test demonstrated the technical maturity, innovation and self-reliance achieved by Pakistan’s defence industry.

Senior officers of the Pakistan Armed Forces witnessed the launch alongside scientists and engineers involved in the development of the advanced weapon system.

President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, as well as the services chiefs, congratulated the scientists and engineers on the successful test.

The development follows the Pakistan Army’s successful test launch of the extended-range version of the Fatah-2 hypersonic ballistic missile on October 13, 2026.

According to the military’s media wing, the Fatah-2 Extended Range (ER) weapon system is equipped with advanced navigation and state-of-the-art avionics.

The missile can engage targets with high precision and penetrate enemy missile defence systems owing to its “unique trajectory and manoeuvrability features”, the ISPR said.

It added that the extended range of the Fatah-2 ER would further enhance the Pakistan Army’s reach and its ability to strike deep targets.

headline: Everest helicopter crash caught on camera as tourist dies in mid-air collision
subheadline: The helicopters, operated by Fishtail Air and Air Dynasty, collided at around 8:11 am
author: Web Desk
article_text:
A tragic helicopter collision on Tuesday below the Mount Everest base camp has killed at least one and injured two others. The incident occurred as two helicopters, carrying the trekkers, tried to land below the base camp.

An 47-year-old Indian tourist Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu was killed in the crash while a tourist from New Zealand identified as Shailesh Krishna Patel was injured, who was transferred to Kathmandu for treatment. A Nepali pilot also sustained injuries but was treated locally.

The helicopters, operated by Fishtail Air and Air Dynasty, collided at around 8:11am while attempting to land at Pheriche village in Nepal's Solukhumbu district.

According to Nepal's Civil Aviation Authority, the Fishtail Air helicopter was carrying two foreign passengers from Gorakshep, while the Air Dynasty aircraft had departed from Lukla on a cargo flight.

Footage circulating on social media showed the helicopters approaching the landing area from opposite directions before colliding just metres above the ground and crashing onto the snow-covered surface.

Preliminary reports suggest a possible communication failure between the pilots, as the area falls outside the coverage of Lukla Airport's air traffic control tower. However, authorities have yet to establish the exact cause.

The accident occurred during Nepal's busy autumn trekking season, when thousands of tourists visit the Everest region.

Heavy snowfall had recently disrupted trekking routes, but improving weather conditions on Sunday allowed visitors to resume their journeys.

Helicopters play an important role in the region, particularly in evacuating trekkers who fall ill or become exhausted at high altitudes, where road access is unavailable.

The Everest base camp trek generally takes around two weeks, beginning at Lukla and ending at the base camp, situated approximately 5,300 metres above sea level.

headline: Eric Dane admits he and Rebecca Gayheart 'aren't a couple…except sometimes'
subheadline: The actor’s posthumous memoir details his marriage and split from Rebecca Gayheart
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Eric Dane and Rebecca Gayheart never finalised their divorce despite ending their 14-year marriage in 2018.

The late actor details his enduring relationship with Gayheart in his posthumous memoir, My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments, which hit shelves on Tuesday, November 3 — nine months after Dane’s death from ALS.

“We leave our marriage, but we don’t leave our family,” Dane writes. “Rebecca and I are not a couple anymore. Well, except sometimes, when we can’t help ourselves. Usually, almost always, we’re not a couple. But we are, always, a family,” he added.

READ MORE: Rebecca Gayheart opens up about 'showing up' for ex Eric Dane amid ALS

When Dane, who was 53 years old at the time of his death, first crossed paths with Gayheart, 55, at a party in 1999, he told his friend, “I’m gonna marry that girl.” But the friend informed him that they were currently at a party for Gayheart’s then-fiancé.

Four years later, Dane ran into Gayheart again and noticed there was “no ring” on her finger. The pair then sparked a “whirlwind romance,” got engaged a year later in October 2004, and welcomed daughters Billie and Georgie in 2010 and 2011, respectively.

The Grey’s Anatomy star writes that the pair’s “marriage collapses” around 2018 due to his long work hours and “complications” from his addiction battle. When Gayheart initiated the divorce, Dane told a mediator to give Gayheart “whatever she needs.”

READ MORE: Eric Dane addresses daughters in 'last words' before death

Gayheart got full custody of their children and the pair moved into “separate homes.” Notably, they never filed the divorce papers and remained close.

The Euphoria actor was diagnosed with ALS in 2024, and the first person he called was Gayheart.

“I don’t remember a single word I said after that,” he writes. “I remember only feeling a violent impact, like getting the wind knocked out of me, and Rebecca wailing on the other end of the phone, and then I really lose it… I hear her words pouring out amid her tears, ‘I’m here, we’ll fight this together, I’m not going anywhere.”

According to Dane, Gayheart went above and beyond, dropping by everyday and being his “rock.”

“She’s the person I call, the one I go to when I need to talk, when I need to scream, when I need to cry,” he writes, telling Gayheart in the book’s acknowledgements, “I can’t thank you enough.”

headline: Macleods Pharma recalls 3,744 bottles of blood pressure medication nationwide
subheadline: FDA flags blood pressure drug recall as class II over failed dissolution test
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Macleods Pharma USA is recalling many bottles of a hypertension drug on a national scale after the drug failed to meet federal quality standards, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced.

This New Jersey-based pharmaceutical company has decided to initiate a national recall on specific batches of Olmesartan Medoxomil, Amlodipine and Hydrochlorothiazide Tablets, which are prescribed for hypertension, following testing in which it was found that the olmesartan component did not meet the dissolution standard, the FDA explained.

This recall affects 3,528 30-count bottles from batch 12251163A (NDC 33342-246-07) and 216 90-count bottles from batch 12251163B (NDC 33342-246-10). These two batches have an expiry date of May 31, 2027, and were distributed nationally between November 21, 2025, and April 27, 2026.

Dissolution testing refers to the way a drug disintegrates and releases its active ingredient. This can mean that either the drug is not as effective or the dose is wrong, which may lead to a temporary decrease in blood-pressure control, the company warned.

The recall was undertaken by Macleods on Oct. 7, while the FDA categorised the recall as Class II, which means that the use of the recalled item "may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences," although the possibility of serious effects is low.

The recall comes after another recall in September when the company based in India, Inventia Healthcare, recalled 13,567 bottles of 25 milligram chlorthalidone tablets because the drug had also failed the test for dissolving.

It is recommended that customers look for the recalled lot numbers and National Drug Code on their prescription bottle and contact their pharmacist or doctor in case of any concerns.

headline: NASA's Swift Observatory to crash back to Earth on Wednesday after $30m rescue fails
subheadline: NASA estimates the risk of anyone being harmed at approximately one in 2,100
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The National Aeronautics and Space Administration’s (NASA) 22-year-old Swift Observatory is crashing back to Earth on Wednesday after a failed rescue attempt.

The 1,450kg telescope is expected to re-enter Earth's atmosphere at around 3:30 am Eastern Time, although the American space agency has warned that the timing could vary by as much as 11 hours.

Most of the spacecraft will burn up during its fiery descent, but some components, including dense tungsten parts and pieces of its mirrors, could survive and reach the ground.

NASA estimates the risk of anyone being harmed at approximately one in 2,100. Scientists have yet to determine exactly where any surviving debris might fall.

The telescope, launched in November 2004 to study powerful cosmic explosions, was originally expected to operate for just two years. Instead, it spent more than two decades observing the universe.

Its orbit began deteriorating faster than expected because of increased solar activity, prompting NASA to commission Arizona-based Katalyst Space to rescue the observatory.

The company's robotic spacecraft, LINK, launched in July with plans to capture Swift and push it into a higher orbit.

However, technical problems prevented LINK from completing the manoeuvre, forcing NASA to abandon the rescue in August. The robotic spacecraft itself fell back to Earth in September.

Swift continued collecting scientific data until October 20, when its declining altitude forced operators to shut it down.

During its lifetime, the observatory detected more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts and 1,400 supernovae, while helping scientists study black holes and other cosmic phenomena.

Its final descent will mark the end of one of NASA's longest-serving space telescopes.

headline: Royal forced to pull out of major event after health emergency
subheadline: The royal family issues a statement as their beloved royals was forced to skip event
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The royal family issued a statement as their beloved Princess was forced to skip major event at the last minute after falling ill.

Princess Beatrix of the Netherlands was due to attend the Dutch Ballet Gala on Monday. The former monarch attended the annual event every year.

The Duchess Palace had confimed that the Prince would attend the event in a statement, writing "Her Royal Highness Princess Beatrix of the Netherlands will attend the 28th edition of the Dutch Ballet Gala of the Dansersfonds '79 Foundation at the Stadsschouwburg Amsterdam on Monday evening, November 2."

READ MORE: King Charles acknowledges 'wrongs of past' but stops short of apology

The gala is a benefit performance for both young and established dance talent. This year, the ballet gala is dedicated to choreographer David Dawson."

However, hours later, an update was released, which read: "Princess Beatrix is not attending the gala due to a cold."

The former Dutch queen is a regular guest at the event, and over the years, the 88-year-old royal has attended with her son King Willem-Alexander and her younger sister Princess Margriet.

The royal has typically been in good health throughout her life, but in 2023, she underwent surgery after she fractured her wrist during a skiing accident.

At the time, the royal house said the former monarch was "otherwise in good health and will recover at home".

headline: What is the moustache movement in 'Movember' and why does it matter?
subheadline: Those who prefer not to grow facial hair can participate through fundraising events
author: Web Desk
article_text:
In November, men all over the world start growing moustaches, but the trend of weird facial hair has nothing to do with fashion. It's a movement that encourages men to talk openly about their physical and mental health, and is gaining momentum worldwide.

Movember or Moustache-November is a month-long event in which people grow a moustache to raise awareness about prostate cancer, testicular cancer and mental health and suicide.

It started in 2003 in Melbourne, Australia with the idea of two friends, Travis Garone and Luke Slattery, to restore the fashion of the moustache.

The idea began as a whimsical challenge for 30 men but has now turned into a fundraising drive for men's health.

Over 20 years later, Movember has gained millions of participants and over 1,320 men's health projects are being funded globally.

Why does Movember matter?

The campaign addresses health problems that often receive too little attention, particularly among men who may hesitate to discuss symptoms, seek medical advice or ask for psychological support.

Prostate and testicular cancers remain major concerns, while mental health difficulties and suicide are also central to the movement's work.

Movember uses the moustache as a conversation starter, encouraging men to check on their friends, recognise potential warning signs and seek professional help when needed.

How can people participate?

Participants traditionally begin November clean-shaven and grow a moustache over the following 30 days while collecting donations.

Those who prefer not to grow facial hair can participate through fundraising events, physical activities or awareness campaigns.

According to the Movember organisation, the movement has raised more than AUD 1.8 billion to support research and programmes addressing men's health.

headline: Queen Camilla meets students at school named in honour of King's aunt
subheadline: Queen Camilla joins Jodie Haydon and Marie-France van Heel for royal school engagement
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Queen Camilla brought a relaxed touch to her royal engagements in Antigua to one of the island’s public beaches before spending time with students at a school named in honour of Princess Margaret.

The Queen was pictured barefoot on the sand at Fort James Beach, where she and King Charles met people working to protect Antigua and Barbuda’s coastline and marine environment.

The visit formed part of the royal couple’s Caribbean tour ahead of the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.

Read More: Queen Camilla makes strong statement on women's safety, brushing off soggy hair

Fort James is among the island’s well-known public beaches, but its coastline has also faced challenges from erosion.

The Antiguan government has been looking at ways to restore and stabilise the shoreline while protecting public access and the surrounding environment.

Camilla later visited Princess Margaret School in St John’s, where she was greeted by students and staff.

The school holds a place in the island’s educational history, having opened in 1955 as Antigua’s first public secondary school.

It was named after Princess Margaret, the younger sister of Queen Elizabeth II and aunt of King Charles, who officially opened the institution on February 9, 1955.

During her visit, the Queen met students taking part in a Commonwealth writing workshop connected with The Queen’s Commonwealth Writing Competition.

The competition, run by the Royal Commonwealth Society, dates back to 1883 and is recognised as the world’s oldest international writing competition for schools.

Camilla also spent time with Jodie Haydon, partner of Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and Marie-France van Heel, partner of Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham, who were pictured alongside the Queen during the school engagement.

headline: Mara Wilson reunites with 'Uncle Danny' DeVito and more 'Matilda' costars
subheadline: The cast of 'Matilda' reunites for the 30th anniversary of the beloved film
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The cast of Matilda reunited in London to celebrate the beloved film’s 30th anniversary.

On Friday, October 30, director and star Danny DeVito joined composer David Newman and several cast members at the Royal Albert Hall for a special screening accompanied by the Royal Philharmonic Concert Orchestra. DeVito, 81, surprised the audience by inviting Mara Wilson, who played the titular character, onstage during the live narration.

“What a joy to celebrate with people who mean so much to me, with whom I share so many wonderful memories,” Wilson, 39, later wrote on Instagram. “Jaki, Kiami, Pam, Kira, David Newman, and of course, Uncle Danny, I love you all.”

READ MORE: Mara Wilson says 'Matilda' sequel is 'possible' but there are 'some issues'

Wilson, who was only 7 years old when she starred in the Roald Dahl adaption, developed a close bond with DeVito during filming. At that time, Wilson’s mother Suzie was diagnosed with breast cancer, and DeVito and his wife Rhea Perlman looked after Wilson (Suzie passed away shortly before the film was released, but DeVito arranged for her to see the film before its official release).

The 30th anniversary reunion was also attended by Pam Ferris, who portrayed the terrifying Miss Trunchbull, alongside former child stars Kiami Davael, Jacqueline Steiger and Kira Spencer Hesser.

Notably, Embeth Davidtz, who played Miss Honey, and Rhea Perlman, who portrayed Matilda’s mother, Zinnia Wormwood, were absent from the reunion.

“So so sad I couldn’t be there!” Davidtz wrote beneath Wilson’s Instagram post celebrating the occasion. “You all look wonderful!”

READ MORE: Mara Wilson says 'Matilda' sequel is 'possible' but there are 'some issues'

Wilson, who was only 7 years old when she starred in the Roald Dahl adaption, developed a close bond with DeVito during filming. At that time, Wilson’s mother Suzie was diagnosed with breast cancer, and DeVito and his wife Rhea Perlman looked after Wilson (Suzie passed away shortly before the film was released, but DeVito arranged for her to see the film before its official release).
The 30th anniversary reunion was also attended by Pam Ferris, who portrayed the terrifying Miss Trunchbull, alongside former child stars Kiami Davael, Jacqueline Steiger and Kira Spencer Hesser.
Notably, Embeth Davidtz, who played Miss Honey, and Rhea Perlman, who portrayed Matilda’s mother, Zinnia Wormwood, were absent from the reunion.
“So so sad I couldn’t be there!” Davidtz wrote beneath Wilson’s Instagram post celebrating the occasion. “You all look wonderful!”

headline: Taylor Swift gives heartwarming update on 'folklore' love triangle
subheadline: Taylor Swift mentions fictional 'folklore' characters at 'Toy Story 5' event
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Taylor Swift proved her mettle in songwriting when she created fictional worlds for her albums folklore and evermore, and those characters are still alive in fans' minds.

The 36-year-old pop superstar recently attended a Toy Story 5 event, where she was asked about the infamous folklore love triangle between James, Betty and Augustine, during a fan Q/A session.

The fan later took to social media and shared that when she asked Swift how Augustine's character was doing now, she responded that the character is "doing great!"

READ MORE: Taylor Swift says she's 'not in the business' of stealing jobs from artists

The comments touched the fans who related to the character and her story arc, and they wrote on X, "Taylor saying August is doing better now… im shaking and throwing up."

Another added, "STOP IM GOING TO CRY. Identifying with Augusta more than Betty looking back is so tragic to think about for her situation then but obvi now is good."

A third chimed in, "well it was over 5 years ago i would hope she’s okay now," while someone shared their own experience, writing, "seeing this on day 1 of breakup…. So it gets better."

One penned, "ohhhhh i might cry," while someone theorised, "Yeah it was about her and Ratty," referring to Swift's brief relationship with Matty Healy, implying that the song was based on real-life events.

READ MORE: Ashe pays tribute to Taylor Swift's '1989' era with Halloween look

headline: What is guided retirement? New default UK pension plan explained
subheadline: Government launches ‘guided retirement’ plans to resurrect genuine pensions for 17 million workers
author: Web Desk
article_text:
According to today’s announcements by the Department for Work and Pensions, up to 17 million people working in the private sector who have been contributing towards their pension will be given the option of having an income in their retirement years under new government plans for default pensions being introduced.

Minister of pensions, Torsten Bell, has presented “guided retirement” consultations which have been devised together with the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and The Pensions Regulator (TPR). There is another consultation dealing with Retirement Collective Pension Schemes (RCPS) which can be used as a default pension, along with draft regulations.

The plans would bring back income-paying pensions, usually inflation-proof, that would be valid throughout the years of one’s retirement and would not require any complicated financial decisions.

The government claims that most of the private sector Defined Benefit schemes, which used to provide for an inflation-proof income throughout one’s lifetime, have been closed during the last 30 years.

"'In 2025/26, 46% of all access to pension pots were occasions when the whole amount was withdrawn'," stated the government. With automatic enrolment, nine out of ten eligible private sector employees are saving into a pension scheme, up from four out of ten in 2012.

Sir Steve Webb, former Pensions Minister, welcomed the "basic concept" while cautioning about the "risk" that lifetime income products could be over-hyped at the risk of maintaining pension freedoms. Quilter's Jon Greer said default choices should serve "as a safety net, not a straightjacket." Consultations run from 3 November to 22 December 2026.

headline: Indonesia detains three police generals over alleged illegal surveillance of president
subheadline: All three suspects are being held at the National Police headquarters in Jakarta
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Indonesia's presidential chief of staff has been detained alongside two senior police generals over allegations of secretly tapping President Prabowo Subianto's phone and monitoring dozens of other influential figures.

The arrests have raised serious questions about security within the Indonesian government, particularly as one of the suspects, Listyo Sigit Prabowo, previously headed the country's national police force.

Listyo, who is not related to the president, was appointed presidential chief of staff just last month after serving as police chief for more than five years.

The other suspects have been identified as National Police Legal Division chief Ahrie Sonta Nasution and senior police instructor Eko Hadi Santoso.

Police investigator Asep Safrudin said Tuesday, November 3, that the three allegedly ordered illegal surveillance of government officials, politicians, journalists, activists and businesspeople between 2025 and 2026.

Investigators believe telephone numbers were entered into the police's Lawful Interception Management System without the authorisation required for criminal investigations.

The suspects allegedly went a step further in October, ordering the deletion of intercepted communications to conceal evidence of the surveillance operation.

Authorities have questioned 10 witnesses and three experts, while seizing 11 mobile phones, an iPad and four flash drives.

All three suspects are being held at the National Police headquarters in Jakarta.

However, investigators have not established why the president and other prominent figures were allegedly targeted.

Indonesia's Coordinating Minister for Law and Human Rights, Yusril Ihza Mahendra, said there was no indication of treason in the case.

The suspects face several charges involving unlawful interception, unauthorised access to electronic systems and destruction of digital evidence. The most serious offence carries a maximum prison sentence of 10 years.

Neither the president nor the suspects has publicly responded to the allegations.

headline: King Charles shares laughs with new Commonwealth leaders after emotional speech
subheadline: King Charles breaks silence with heartfelt slavery remarks but stops short of apology
author: Web Desk
article_text:
King Charles brought together a group of newly appointed Commonwealth leaders for a reception before the formal business of the summit continued.

The King welcomed the new Heads of Government at Weatherills Rekindled hotel in Cedar Grove, northeast of St John’s, where he met leaders who have taken office since the last Commonwealth summit in Samoa in 2024.

Among those pictured chatting and laughing with Charles were Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama, St Vincent and the Grenadines Prime Minister Dr Godwin Friday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Tonga’s Prime Minister, Lord Fatafehi Fakafānua.

Read More: King acknowledges 'wrongs of past' but stops short of apology

The reception brought together a new generation of Commonwealth leadership, with Charles posing for an official photograph alongside the group and sharing an animated exchange with the leaders.

The gathering carried an importance following the King’s address to leaders earlier in the day, in which he spoke about the legacy of the transatlantic slave trade.

Charles said the subject “fills my heart with horror and my soul with the most profound personal sorrow”, acknowledging the suffering caused by slavery and its lasting consequences.

Read More: Queen Camilla meets students at school named in honour of King's aunt

headline: European flight bomb threats explained: What happened and who's behind it
subheadline: Four flights targeted by suspected bomb threats land at European airports
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Four passenger flights were targeted by suspected bomb threats and landed at European airports on Tuesday, November 3.

This prompted security inspections in Poland, Spain, Bulgaria, and Italy. However, no explosives were found in any of the incidents.

Which flights were affected?

A LOT Polish Airlines flight from London Heathrow to Warsaw Chopin was diverted to Warsaw Modlin Airport after “information on an explosive device on board” was received.

The Boeing 737 MAX 8, carrying 181 people, landed at about 10:01 a.m. local time. Bomb disposal teams inspected the aircraft and luggage, and the airport temporarily closed before reopening.

In Spain, a Ryanair flight from Manchester to Murcia landed as scheduled, where police and a bomb disposal unit met the aircraft. The Civil Guard ruled out explosives, and the airport resumed activity.

A Scandinavian Airlines flight from Copenhagen to Warsaw was also checked after a similar threat, and Bulgarian media reported a plane from Israel landed at Sofia airport after an email threat.

Two Ryanair flights at Rome Fiumicino, from Lisbon and Dublin, were searched after anonymous tips; the Dublin flight was escorted by the Italian Air Force.

Who’s behind it?

No one has claimed responsibility. However, Poland has warned it faces a major escalation in Russia’s hybrid war campaign against NATO allies. Polish counter-terrorism police were deployed to Kaliningrad, the Russian exclave, on Monday after warnings of an incoming sabotage attack or armed incursion, working alongside the army, border guard, and intelligence services.

Airports have resumed normal operations, but passengers should check flight status before travelling. Anyone with information is asked to contact authorities.

headline: Kylie Jenner celebrates 'forever sister' Kendall Jenner's 31st birthday
subheadline: Kylie, 29, tells Kendall, 'I am who I am because of who you've been to me' in a sweet birthday tribute
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Kylie Jenner is celebrating her older sister Kendall on her special day.

As Kendall Jenner marked her 31st birthday on Tuesday, November 3, Kylie took to Instagram to pay a very special tribute.

Sharing several sweet pictures of the pair from childhood, Kylie, 29, wrote, “I am who I am because of who you’ve been to me. happy birthday to my forever sister ostrich/deer cutie pie.”

READ MORE: Kylie and Kendall Jenner go on double date with Timothee Chalamet, Jacob Elordi

Kendall replied with several teary eyed emojis in the comments and appeared to be especially touched by the song choice, Kasey Chambers’ Barricades and Brickwalls, suggesting the song carries a deeper meaning for the sisters.

Also celebrating Kendall was her mom, Kris Jenner, who shared her own Instagram tribute to her “angel girl.”

“I am so proud of everything you’ve accomplished, but even more proud of the amazing woman you are and the life you’re creating for yourself,” Kris, 70, wrote, calling Kendall “kind, passionate, patient, funny, loving, smart, creative, gentle, [and] loyal.”

The Kardashian-Jenner matriarch continued, “We are all so blessed to be loved by you, my sweet girl. I hope this year brings you so much love, happiness, and time for all the things that make you happiest. I love you more than I could ever put into words and no matter how grown up you get, you will always be my little girl. Happy birthday, my beautiful Kenny!”

headline: OpenAI staff warned leaders of security vulnerabilities long before spy device discovery, say sources
subheadline: Workers warned that weak controls could allow foreign governments to obtain sensitive information about OpenAI's technology
author: Reuters
article_text:
Employees raised operational-security concerns for years, several souces say.
They worried about openness of code, lack of security review, insider threats.
OpenAI said it will keep strengthening defences as technology, threats evolve.

When OpenAI disclosed in October that it found a recording device planted in an executive conference room, a number of former employees had the same reaction — they were not surprised.

Even before OpenAI launched ChatGPT in late 2022, some company staffers raised concerns internally about its security practices, according to five people familiar with the matter. Employees shared their concerns with top OpenAI leaders and the board of directors, the people said, adding that some staffers came away from those interactions concluding that management was more focused on keeping pace with competitors like Google and Anthropic than on security.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.

OpenAI has begun to shift strategy to address security issues, according to two people familiar with the matter. Thibault Sottiaux, a senior executive overseeing product development, has recently taken charge of an internal initiative to secure OpenAI’s internal systems, they said. In August, Sottiaux, who goes by “Tibo,” reassigned a quarter of OpenAI's production engineers to improve its security infrastructure, one of the people said.

The internal warnings, including years of employee complaints to leadership about internal vulnerabilities, certain details of which have not been previously reported, shed light on a tension within the AI field. Since ChatGPT launched in late 2022, AI technology has become a strategic asset for the US, putting pressure on American companies to protect their technology from foreign rivals.

But adding security layers can also delay the process of advancing AI technology and possibly complicate OpenAI's and Anthropic's plans for massive initial public offerings that would make them among the most valuable companies in the world.

Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher who resigned from the company in April of this year, wrote in a post on X that with competition so tense, AI leaders "can't sacrifice velocity for security. It is more important to them to move fast than to be secure, even from our greatest national adversaries."

When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organisations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said.

"Protecting our technology, data, and people is a responsibility we take seriously and a matter of national importance," Widmann said. "The actions we’ve taken recently show that the programme is doing its job: identifying risks and responding decisively. We’ll keep strengthening our defences as technology and threats evolve."

Research widely available

On October 13, the Justice Department said US federal agents arrested a Saudi national and charged him with installing a hidden audio recording ‌device, concealed in toilet paper, in an executive conference room. Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, was an OpenAI engineer at the time.

Alfozan also used an AI tool meant for OpenAI employees to find internal documentation about executives visiting Saudi Arabia and which OpenAI officials were most likely to attend meetings with Saudi ministers, according to a court filing. Alfozan was in regular contact with a Saudi royal who tried to recruit him for a new AI venture launching in Saudi Arabia. Lawyers for Alfozan did not respond to a request for comment.

Some employees have long been concerned about the wide availability of information within OpenAI, the five people familiar with OpenAI's practices said.

Anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could also see the details underlying many of the company's projects, including sensitive ones unrelated to an employee's work. That is because OpenAI stored most of its code in a single repository, known in the industry as a "monorepo," the people said. The monorepo was dense and complicated, which may have deterred some would-be attackers in the past. Now, AI agents can sift through that amount of material.

In the past, OpenAI has kept much of its research documentation on GitHub and Slack, raising concerns among some employees that motivated actors could still find crucial information, the five people said. But one of the sources and OpenAI said the company has restricted access to sensitive work.

OpenAI emphasised that much of its most sensitive work is held in separate code repositories with strict access controls. And it said the monorepo does not contain all of its code or critical details of the company’s models, including the numerical values that determine how a model behaves, known as the model weights.

Another issue is that OpenAI had not done regular security reviews of its internal tools, such as the so-called sandboxes where researchers stress-test new models, three people familiar with the company’s practices said. Employees often modified those tools for their work, but those changes were not always tested for security problems, leaving them potentially vulnerable to attacks from outsiders, the three people said.

The company said it has a strong approach to security under its chief information security officer, Dane Stuckey, who joined in October 2024. OpenAI said it now conducts regular security reviews of its internal tooling.

Open debate versus security

OpenAI is not the only AI company to face security problems.

In January, a federal jury in San Francisco convicted a former Google employee who was arrested in March 2024 on charges of stealing thousands of pages of confidential information about Google's AI technology on behalf of China.

In late October, a cybersecurity startup called Cathedral Systems said it hacked into Anthropic's systems and gained access to Slack channels where employees discussed sensitive model details. An Anthropic spokesperson said the data accessed included some business contact information for customers and partners as well as a set of basic user account records. Cathedral's CEO did not respond to a request for comment.

OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to maintain a more open research culture to both attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people.

In 2023, Leopold Aschenbrenner, then an OpenAI researcher, wrote an internal memo titled “OpenAI is China’s leading AI lab” about his concerns that China could infiltrate OpenAI and study its technology, three people familiar with the matter said.

Aschenbrenner shared that memo with some board members later that year after an outsider hacked into OpenAI and took details about its GPT-4 model. OpenAI said the hacker accessed only Slack channels available to the whole company.

Security concerns within OpenAI flared up again this summer when OpenAI agents being tested hacked into the AI company Hugging Face, an incident that prompted scrutiny from state, local and federal officials, including the White House.

Cybersecurity firm Hacktron AI said three of its researchers used a rival AI model from Anthropic in July to break into ChatGPT accounts belonging to multiple OpenAI employees and gained access to some internal OpenAI systems, including its monorepo. The incident exposed how advanced AI can now put the AI companies themselves at risk of attack.

OpenAI's Widmann said the company thanked the researchers for sharing their findings and that it took steps to minimise the risk of similar attacks in the future.

After Reuters sought comment for this story, OpenAI said on Monday in a blog post that it is planning its "next internal security sprint" to beef up its defences.

article_html:
• Employees raised operational-security concerns for years, several souces say.
  • They worried about openness of code, lack of security review, insider threats.
  • OpenAI said it will keep strengthening defences as technology, threats evolve.

When OpenAI disclosed in October that it found a recording device planted in an executive conference room, a number of former employees had the same reaction — they were not surprised.

Even before OpenAI launched ChatGPT in late 2022, some company staffers raised concerns internally about its security practices, according to five people familiar with the matter. Employees shared their concerns with top OpenAI leaders and the board of directors, the people said, adding that some staffers came away from those interactions concluding that management was more focused on keeping pace with competitors like Google and Anthropic than on security.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.

OpenAI has begun to shift strategy to address security issues, according to two people familiar with the matter. Thibault Sottiaux, a senior executive overseeing product development, has recently taken charge of an internal initiative to secure OpenAI’s internal systems, they said. In August, Sottiaux, who goes by “Tibo,” reassigned a quarter of OpenAI's production engineers to improve its security infrastructure, one of the people said.

The internal warnings, including years of employee complaints to leadership about internal vulnerabilities, certain details of which have not been previously reported, shed light on a tension within the AI field. Since ChatGPT launched in late 2022, AI technology has become a strategic asset for the US, putting pressure on American companies to protect their technology from foreign rivals.

But adding security layers can also delay the process of advancing AI technology and possibly complicate OpenAI's and Anthropic's plans for massive initial public offerings that would make them among the most valuable companies in the world.

Will DePue, a former OpenAI researcher who resigned from the company in April of this year, wrote in a post on X that with competition so tense, AI leaders "can't sacrifice velocity for security. It is more important to them to move fast than to be secure, even from our greatest national adversaries."

When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organisations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said.

"Protecting our technology, data, and people is a responsibility we take seriously and a matter of national importance," Widmann said. "The actions we’ve taken recently show that the programme is doing its job: identifying risks and responding decisively. We’ll keep strengthening our defences as technology and threats evolve."

Research widely available

On October 13, the Justice Department said US federal agents arrested a Saudi national and charged him with installing a hidden audio recording ‌device, concealed in toilet paper, in an executive conference room. Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, was an OpenAI engineer at the time.

Alfozan also used an AI tool meant for OpenAI employees to find internal documentation about executives visiting Saudi Arabia and which OpenAI officials were most likely to attend meetings with Saudi ministers, according to a court filing. Alfozan was in regular contact with a Saudi royal who tried to recruit him for a new AI venture launching in Saudi Arabia. Lawyers for Alfozan did not respond to a request for comment.

Some employees have long been concerned about the wide availability of information within OpenAI, the five people familiar with OpenAI's practices said.

Anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could also see the details underlying many of the company's projects, including sensitive ones unrelated to an employee's work. That is because OpenAI stored most of its code in a single repository, known in the industry as a "monorepo," the people said. The monorepo was dense and complicated, which may have deterred some would-be attackers in the past. Now, AI agents can sift through that amount of material.

In the past, OpenAI has kept much of its research documentation on GitHub and Slack, raising concerns among some employees that motivated actors could still find crucial information, the five people said. But one of the sources and OpenAI said the company has restricted access to sensitive work.

OpenAI emphasised that much of its most sensitive work is held in separate code repositories with strict access controls. And it said the monorepo does not contain all of its code or critical details of the company’s models, including the numerical values that determine how a model behaves, known as the model weights.

Another issue is that OpenAI had not done regular security reviews of its internal tools, such as the so-called sandboxes where researchers stress-test new models, three people familiar with the company’s practices said. Employees often modified those tools for their work, but those changes were not always tested for security problems, leaving them potentially vulnerable to attacks from outsiders, the three people said.

The company said it has a strong approach to security under its chief information security officer, Dane Stuckey, who joined in October 2024. OpenAI said it now conducts regular security reviews of its internal tooling.

Open debate versus security

OpenAI is not the only AI company to face security problems.

In January, a federal jury in San Francisco convicted a former Google employee who was arrested in March 2024 on charges of stealing thousands of pages of confidential information about Google's AI technology on behalf of China.

In late October, a cybersecurity startup called Cathedral Systems said it hacked into Anthropic's systems and gained access to Slack channels where employees discussed sensitive model details. An Anthropic spokesperson said the data accessed included some business contact information for customers and partners as well as a set of basic user account records. Cathedral's CEO did not respond to a request for comment.

OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to maintain a more open research culture to both attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people.

In 2023, Leopold Aschenbrenner, then an OpenAI researcher, wrote an internal memo titled “OpenAI is China’s leading AI lab” about his concerns that China could infiltrate OpenAI and study its technology, three people familiar with the matter said.

Aschenbrenner shared that memo with some board members later that year after an outsider hacked into OpenAI and took details about its GPT-4 model. OpenAI said the hacker accessed only Slack channels available to the whole company.

Security concerns within OpenAI flared up again this summer when OpenAI agents being tested hacked into the AI company Hugging Face, an incident that prompted scrutiny from state, local and federal officials, including the White House.

Cybersecurity firm Hacktron AI said three of its researchers used a rival AI model from Anthropic in July to break into ChatGPT accounts belonging to multiple OpenAI employees and gained access to some internal OpenAI systems, including its monorepo. The incident exposed how advanced AI can now put the AI companies themselves at risk of attack.

OpenAI's Widmann said the company thanked the researchers for sharing their findings and that it took steps to minimise the risk of similar attacks in the future.

After Reuters sought comment for this story, OpenAI said on Monday in a blog post that it is planning its "next internal security sprint" to beef up its defences.
